# Execution Feedback and Correction

| [AM.MAN.DEX.VLA.FEEDBACK.1] <a id="am-man-dex-vla-feedback-1"></a> | [AgenticTactileVLA: Contact-Guided Execution-Time Supervision for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation without VLA Retraining](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04391v1)<br>Elizaveta Semenyakina et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `vla` `execution-feedback` `action-correction` `proprioception` `contact-estimation` `compliant-control` `grasping` `pick-and-place` `real-world` | **Feedback/correction:** After nominal VLA finger closure, detect contact evidence from commanded-versus-measured finger motion and, during correction, motor-effort feedback. If support is insufficient, pause body-reference progression while maintaining stabilization and advance unsupported fingers independently until contact. Retain the corrected hand configuration when support criteria pass; otherwise return control to the VLA for retry.<br>**Where it acts:** An external, nonlearned supervisor changes executed commands; the corrected hand state enters subsequent VLA observations without updating VLA parameters. The base VLA was fine-tuned on teleoperated demonstrations.<br>**Compliant mode:** Before closure, language cues or a VLM select predefined current-limited control for fragile objects. No additional tactile sensors are required; motor feedback is not calibrated contact force.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Unitree G1 with BrainCo Revo2 and fixed GR00T-N1.6-3B; five held-out objects, 15 matched trials per object, with a shared 60-second/three-approach budget. Completion rises from 61.3% for the base VLA to 84.0% (72.0% for unconditional close-to-stall). The compliant branch evaluates object integrity during closure and holding, not autonomous transport; cross-hand and cross-VLA generality are not established. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04391v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-22 |
